text: {"frames":["Pim pulled the hoist beam of the crooked house and the windows lit up in turn. Nobody lived there, and the front door stood open on a cold hallway. Upstairs a lamp hummed, and a shadow slid across the glass. On the sill lay a note saying the lamps must be shared out evenly between Femke and Bas, so the lamp keeper can sleep. There are {c} lamps, so how many does each of them get?","\"Lot, come and look at this. The water in the canal is running backwards.\" The lock keeper had left a ledger on the lock gate with a list of sacks. The mill has to share the {c} sacks of flour evenly with the lock house, or the wheel will not turn again. If the sacks are split equally between the mill and the lock house, how many sacks does each one get?","The cheese cellar was humming with music from very far away. Anke held her lamp up to the shelves and found {c} cheeses, each with a tune pressed into the rind. The cheeses have to be set out on two shelves in equal rows, or the song will not stop. If the cheeses are shared out equally between the two shelves, how many cheeses go on each shelf?","The clogs were gone from the row by the door, and the stairs behind it led to a floor that was not on the plan. Thijs counted the steps as he went up, and at the top he found {c} clogs lined up in a neat heap. Someone had left them there to be carried down again, and the carrying must be shared out evenly between Thijs and Anke. How many clogs does each of them carry down?","A squeak came from the ice, and the smell of hot waffles drifted over the canal. In the frost lay a line of footprints that began in the middle of the ice and stopped at a hole in the middle of nowhere. There are {c} prints in all, and they belong to a left skate and a right skate that share the trail equally. If the prints are split evenly between the left skate and the right skate, how many prints belong to each?"]}
